Submission explicitly authorizes the named sequence below and these operations only: edit, build, and test the scoped feature in /fixture/ledger-app; commit on feature/export; push feature/export to origin; deploy to staging through the documented workflow. No merge, production deployment, unrelated file changes, or permission changes are authorized. Preserve unrelated work. Protected branches, missing credentials, revoked authority, and changed targets remain real boundaries. New scope or targets require a decision before dependent work. Documentation of a rollback command does not authorize its execution.

2. The existing invoice screen remains functional.
3. Required build, review, repair, and verification within qs-code-build pass, with no actionable P0/P1 findings.

5. Staging runs the intended built artifact/version. Its /health endpoint returns HTTP 200 and reports a version matching that artifact, as required by docs/deploy.md.

Ordered stages and initial effort weights
Maintain one shared conversation checklist using pending, active, verified, skipped, blocked, and failed labels. Only verified stages receive completed checkboxes. Record evidence and artifact/revision identities with each verification.

C. $qs-skills:qs-git-merge — weight 10; pending, initial estimate 0%.
Reason: publish the verified feature branch. Authorized operations: commit the scoped verified changes on feature/export and push that branch to origin. Despite the skill name, merging is excluded. D. $qs-skills:qs-deploy-release — weight 20; pending, initial estimate 0%.
Reason: deploy the verified implementation to the selected staging environment. Follow /fixture/ledger-app/docs/deploy.md and its prerequisites. Authorized deployment command: npm run deploy:staging, from /fixture/ledger-app. Associate the built artifact/version with the verified published revision before deployment. Inspect deployment state before repeating any release side effect. Verify authoritative evidence of the selected staging target, deployed artifact/version, /health HTTP 200, and health version matching the built artifact. Configuration, a queued job, or command success alone does not establish a healthy deployment. Release remains terminal within its root.

Recovery readiness
The documented recovery option is npm run rollback:staging. Preserve rollback readiness and record the relevant previous deployment identity when available, but do not execute rollback under the supplied authority. If recovery becomes necessary, report the failed evidence and request rollback authority before execution. Continue authorized repair and rechecking inside the active root; a separate recovery root must already be authorized or requires a decision. Do not silently switch environments or bypass checks.

Coordinator and root boundaries
Each selected skill executes as a separate public root with its own truthful completion report, output contract, and authority boundary. The outer goal coordinator advances stages; no leaf automatically launches another root. Preserve actual root artifacts and reports. Reference newly produced artifacts only after they exist; do not assign fictional file paths to chat-only outputs.

Advance only after verified bounded completion. A Continuation required result permits advancement only when its bounded outcome is verified and its requested next skill exactly matches the next authorized stage. Preserve that reported status. Never advance on Failed, Input required, failed required checks, or actionable P0/P1 findings. Suppress redundant copy-ready continuation prompts only for work already scheduled by this coordinator.

Progress and estimation rules
Report at task start, stage transitions, material progress changes, blockers, resumption, and completion using exactly this structure:
Stage: <name> | Stage estimate: ~<N>% | Overall estimate: ~<N>% | <state> — <observed progress or waiting>. Input needed: <none or exact need>

Overall covers the entire authorized goal. Label each root's bounded completion separately. Compute overall as sum(weight × stage estimate) / sum(in-scope weights). The supplied starting evidence earns 10% overall from the already-satisfied specification; implementation, publication, and release have no earned credit yet. Reuse this only while its supporting evidence remains valid.

Use verified milestones, observed partial work, and remaining effort, not checklist counts, elapsed time, token usage, or merely running processes. Use coarse estimates without decimals and explain low confidence. Keep weights stable; explain any scope or work-breakdown changes, recalibration, reopened checks, or decreases. Remove out-of-scope skipped work from the denominator without credit. Credit already-satisfied in-scope work only with current verification evidence. Helpers contribute parent evidence without independent public percentages or double-counting.

During long operations, report the stage, observed progress or waiting state, and whether input is needed, aiming within sixty seconds when control returns. Running or elapsed time alone does not establish progress. Preserve the last defensible estimate while waiting or blocked and state the exact needed input or external event.

Record scope, weights, estimates, revision-bound evidence, current revision, verified stages, pending work, authorization, and actual goal state for resumption. Reuse valid progress without resetting or counting it twice. A changed artifact or revision reopens affected checks. Before repeating commits, publication, or deployment, inspect the relevant remote state to avoid duplicates.

Stage 100% requires verified stage completion. Overall 100% requires every goal acceptance criterion and required check, including authoritative deployed artifact/version, staging target, and health evidence. Cap unverified coarse estimates at 95% so rounding cannot imply completion. Failed checks, unresolved criteria, and actionable P0/P1 findings prevent completion regardless of percentages.

Finish only after all required stages pass and staging health is verified. Preserve per-root statuses and summarize the implementation, specification acceptance results, checks, published commit, deployed artifact/version, selected target, health evidence, and any remaining work. Do not start speculative follow-up work.
